```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(heteroTests)
```

This vignette demonstrates the main workflow in greater depth. We use the
`boston_housing` dataset bundled with the package.

```{r}
data(boston_housing, package = "heteroTests")
head(boston_housing)
```

## 1. Fit an initial model

```{r}
base_model <- lm(medv ~ lstat + rm + crim, data = boston_housing)
summary(base_model)
```

## 2. Diagnose heteroscedasticity

```{r}
hd <- HeteroDiagnostic(base_model, boston_housing)
test(hd)
plot(hd)
```

## 3. Apply a remedy

```{r}
wls_model <- fitWLS(base_model)
summary(wls_model)
```

## 4. Compare models

```{r}
compareModelDiagnostics(list(base_model, wls_model))
```

The weighted least squares fit typically reduces the heteroscedasticity metrics.
